title: Error Classification and Handling
description: Classify message processing errors as transient or permanent, and apply the right handling strategy to avoid data loss and infinite loops.

data.text: When a message fails, the first question should be: can this succeed if I try again later? Error classification answers that question. Transient errors such as database deadlocks or API rate limits may resolve with a retry. Permanent errors such as malformed JSON or missing required fields will never succeed and must be handled differently.

Transient errors are temporary conditions. The downstream service is busy, a network partition is healing, or a lock is held for a moment. Permanent errors are structural. The payload is invalid, the business rule is violated, or the target resource does not exist. Routing permanent errors into endless retry cycles wastes compute and clutters the DLQ with poison messages.

rows: Missing required field, invalid business state

data.text: A poison message is a message that always fails processing, regardless of how many times it is retried. It may contain corrupted data, an invalid format, or a reference to a deleted entity. Without proper handling, a poison message can dominate consumer resources and delay all other work.

data.title: Poison Message Risk
data.text: A single poison message can trigger thousands of retry attempts. Always set a hard maximum receive count so the broker moves it to the DLQ before it damages throughput.

data.caption: Error classification and routing decision flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Message Fails] --> B{Classify Error}
    B -->|Transient| C[Retry with Backoff]
    C -->|Still Failing| D[Move to DLQ after Max Retries]
    B -->|Permanent| E[Send to DLQ Immediately]
    D --> F[Human Review or Automated Action]
    E --> F
    style C fill:#fff9c4,stroke:#333
    style E fill:#ffccbc,stroke:#333
    style F fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#333

terms.definition: A message that always fails processing and must be removed from the main queue to protect throughput.
A temporary failure that may succeed if retried after a delay.
A structural or business-rule failure that will not succeed on retry.
The threshold at which a broker moves a message to the DLQ instead of retrying.
